hypothesis: Ares Alpha will exhibit a reproducible failure boundary when compound resource shocks, sustained production loss, low coordination, and capability loss jointly exceed the colony's recovery capacity.
control: Current EXP-CIV-001 baseline scenario under the canonical seed and initial conditions.
sample_or_runs_plan: Run a deterministic parameter sweep across predefined stress levels, then repeat boundary-adjacent configurations across multiple seeds before interpreting a stable boundary.
randomization_plan: The first sweep uses fixed canonical seeds for reproducibility; boundary-adjacent follow-up runs must use multiple declared seeds rather than selecting favorable outcomes.
measurement_plan: Capture one observation per Sol using the existing Experiment Runtime and record every runtime intervention explicitly in the event stream.
analysis_plan: Estimate the transition from recovery to non-recovery by scenario, compare minima and recovery times with baseline, and report the lowest stress configuration that produces persistent collapse without changing the analysis rule after seeing outcomes.
stopping_rule: Do not stop early because a desired boundary is found; complete the predefined sweep and observation window for all scheduled runs unless the runtime reaches an explicit terminal state.
robustness_plan: Repeat near-boundary cases across multiple seeds and vary one stress dimension at a time to test sensitivity and interaction effects.
replication_plan: After an internal multi-seed boundary is identified, require an independent implementation or external model/data comparison before promoting related insights to validated status.
notes: This preregistration governs the next failure-boundary suite. It does not retroactively preregister baseline-001 or comparative-001.
